subject: Science
title: Year 9 Science Exam 3
topic: Inheritance & chemical reactions · AQA Higher · Paper B
intro: Calculator allowed. Relative atomic masses (A<sub>r</sub>): H = 1, O = 16, Mg = 24, Ca = 40. For a method question, write numbered steps someone else could follow, with equipment, measurements and safety. For longer answers write in full sentences and use key words. Describe = say what happens; Explain = say what happens and why (use because and so); Compare = similarities and differences (use whereas); Evaluate = points for and against, then a justified conclusion. 6-mark questions are marked on how well your ideas link together: plan for a minute, then write about 6 linked points.

questions.q:
In guinea pigs, the allele for black fur (B) is dominant over the allele for white fur (b).
Explain the difference between a genotype and a phenotype. Use guinea pig fur colour as an example.
questions.ms: Genotype is the combination of alleles, e.g. Bb (1); phenotype is the characteristic that is expressed, e.g. black fur (1).

questions.q:
A black guinea pig is crossed with a white guinea pig. They have 10 offspring: 5 black and 5 white.
Use a genetic diagram to work out the genotype of the black parent. Explain your answer.
questions.ms: White parent must be bb (1); Bb × bb gives Bb, Bb, bb, bb, a 1 : 1 ratio (1); matches 5 : 5 so the black parent is Bb; if BB all offspring would be black (1).

questions.q: Two guinea pigs with the genotype Bb are crossed. Give the expected ratio of black : white offspring.
Put these structures in order of size, starting with the smallest: cell, chromosome, gene, nucleus.
questions.hint: Type the four words in order, separated by commas
questions.ms: gene → chromosome → nucleus → cell (1).

questions.q: Explain how a mutation could lead to a new characteristic appearing in a population.
questions.ms: A mutation changes the DNA / base sequence of a gene (1); this creates a new allele, which may give a new characteristic / phenotype (1).

questions.q: Fur colour in guinea pigs is an example of discontinuous variation, whereas body mass is an example of continuous variation. Explain the difference between these two types of variation.
questions.ms: Discontinuous falls into distinct groups with no values in between (1), whereas continuous can take any value within a range (1).

questions.q:
Biodiversity is the variety of all the different species of organisms on Earth, or within an ecosystem.
Explain why it is important to maintain biodiversity, and describe techniques that can be used to protect it.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Why: high biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable; species depend on each other (food, shelter, pollination); losing one species affects food webs; humans rely on it for food, medicines, materials. Techniques: breeding programmes; protecting / regenerating habitats (reserves, replanting); field margins and hedgerows; reducing deforestation, pollution and CO₂; recycling; seed / gene banks. Level 3 explains why AND describes several techniques with reasons.

questions.q: Patients are told to complete the full course of antibiotics, even if they feel better. Explain why, using ideas about natural selection.
questions.ms: Some bacteria may be resistant / not all killed yet (1); if stopped early these survivors reproduce (1); pass on the resistance allele so a resistant population develops (1).

questions.q:
The Arabian oryx became extinct in the wild in 1972, mainly because of hunting. Captive breeding programmes, including in the UAE, have since returned it to the wild.
Suggest one reason why a population bred from a small number of captive animals may struggle to survive in the wild. Explain your answer.
questions.ms: Low genetic variation / inbreeding (1), so the whole population could be wiped out by a new disease or environmental change (1). Allow: lack survival behaviours (avoiding predators, finding food) (1) + explanation (1).

questions.q:
When magnesium is heated, it reacts with oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
Describe a method to find the mass of magnesium oxide formed when a known mass of magnesium ribbon is heated in a crucible.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Indicative: weigh empty crucible and lid; add coiled magnesium and reweigh, subtract for mass of Mg; heat strongly on a pipe-clay triangle over a Bunsen; lift lid occasionally with tongs to let oxygen in; keep lid mostly on so MgO smoke doesn't escape; heat until it stops glowing, cool; reweigh and reheat to constant mass; final mass − crucible = mass of MgO; safety: eye protection, don't look at the burning magnesium. Level 3: logical method, how masses are found and why the lid is lifted.

questions.q:
A student heats different masses of magnesium. Her results:
Mass of magnesium (g)0.120.240.360.480.60
Mass of magnesium oxide (g)0.200.400.520.801.00
Identify the anomalous result. Suggest one reason for it.
questions.ms: 0.52 g (for 0.36 g Mg) (1). Reason: some MgO escaped as smoke / not all Mg reacted / not heated to constant mass (1).

questions.q: Name the independent variable and the dependent variable.
questions.ms: Independent: mass of magnesium (1). Dependent: mass of magnesium oxide (1).

questions.q: Calculate the theoretical mass of magnesium oxide that should be made from 0.36 g of magnesium. (g)
questions.ms: 0.60 g. Mg : MgO = 24 : 40 or 48 g → 80 g (1); 0.36 × 40 ÷ 24 = 0.60 g (1). Allow the pattern in the other results (× 5/3).

questions.q: Calculate the percentage yield for the 0.36 g sample. Give your answer to 2 significant figures. (%)
Define the term electrolysis.
questions.ms: Breaking down an ionic compound into simpler substances / elements (1) using an electric current (1).

questions.q: Aluminium is extracted by the electrolysis of aluminium oxide. Explain why the aluminium oxide must be molten (melted) and not solid.
questions.ms: In a solid the ions are fixed / cannot move (1); when molten the ions are free to move and carry the current to the electrodes (1).

questions.q:
Predict whether each reaction will happen. Explain each prediction using the reactivity series.
(a) zinc + copper sulfate
(b) copper + magnesium sulfate
questions.ms: (a) Yes: zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper (1). (b) No: copper is less reactive than magnesium, so it cannot displace it (1).

questions.q: Write a balanced symbol equation for the reaction between zinc (Zn) and copper sulfate (CuSO₄).
questions.ms: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (1).

questions.q:
A catalytic converter changes carbon monoxide and nitrogen monoxide into less harmful gases.
Name the products formed from each gas, and explain why a catalyst is used.
questions.ms: Carbon monoxide → carbon dioxide (1); nitrogen monoxide → nitrogen (and oxygen) (1); a catalyst speeds up the reaction without being used up, so the gases are converted quickly as they pass through (1).

questions.q: Which of these is a functional adaptation?
questions.ms: producing very concentrated urine (1).

questions.q:
The Arabian camel lives in the deserts of the UAE. Daytime temperatures can be above 45 °C, and there is very little water.
Explain how structural, behavioural and functional adaptations help the camel to survive in the desert.
questions.ms: Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): detailed and coherent, points linked in a logical sequence, correct terms. Level 2 (3–4): several relevant points with some linking. Level 1 (1–2): simple, separate statements. 0: nothing relevant. Structural: hump stores fat for energy / water; wide flat feet don't sink in sand; long eyelashes and closable nostrils keep out sand; thick fur on top shades skin. Behavioural: rests in the hottest part of the day; drinks large volumes quickly. Functional: little, concentrated urine and dry faeces; body temperature rises before sweating, saving water. Level 3 includes all three types, each linked to survival.

questions.q: The fennec fox also lives in the desert. It has very large ears. Suggest two ways its large ears help it to survive.
questions.ms: Any two: large surface area to lose heat / keep cool (1); hear prey, e.g. insects underground (1); hear predators coming (1).

questions.q: Hydrogen peroxide has the formula H₂O₂. Give the ratio of hydrogen atoms to oxygen atoms in its simplest form.
How many atoms in total are in one formula unit of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂?
Calculate the relative formula mass (M<sub>r</sub>) of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂.
Which of these is a biotic factor?
questions.ms: availability of prey (1).
